This archive includes working copies of each version of the "MAD Computer" program published in the October 1985 issue of MAD Magazine. APPLE II: mad_apple.dsk is a bootable disk image that runs the program. The graphics routines end up corrupting the program as it runs, so to rerun the program, you will need to reboot the system or enter the command RUN HELLO at the BASIC prompt. ATARI: The disk image includes a BASIC program named MAD.BAS. Configure your emulator to have the ATARI BASIC cartridge attached, then boot mad_atari.atr and enter the command LOAD "D:MAD.BAS" followed by RUN. COMMODORE 64: mad_c64.d64 is a disk image with a BASIC program on it. Most Commodore emulators should be able to successfully autostart it, but without that (or on real hardware) you will need to type LOAD "MAD",8 followed by RUN. This edition is many times slower than the other three (taking approximately 20 minutes to complete) so you will want to make use of any kind of "warp mode" that your emulator provides. DOS: The mad_dos.bas file works unchanged in both GW-BASIC and QuickBASIC. In GW-BASIC enter the command LOAD "MAD_DOS" followed by RUN, and in QuickBASIC open the file in the QuickBASIC environment and then hit F5 to run. This is the simplest implementation of the four, and it also will load as an ordinary text file in any editor; if you wish to experiment with this program, this is the edition you should be looking at.
